question: Given that validity-aware legal retrieval is already prescribed and partially implemented, can a post-hoc temporal re-ranking component still be positioned as a distinct contribution, or is the remaining defensible delta only version-level contamination measurement on near-duplicate amended clauses?
description: Two retrieved legal-domain works already prescribe validity-aware retrieval (bitemporal correctness; ontology filtering by temporal validity) and a legal benchmark already encodes temporal validity. It is unclear whether a lightweight post-hoc temporal re-ranking study can be positioned as a distinct contribution against this line, or whether it is subsumed by deterministic-by-design legal retrieval. Resolving this determines whether to refine the contribution, change the hypothesis toward version-level contamination measurement, or abandon the direction.
confidence_basis: Convergent comparison evidence across five sources: the closest framework reports no empirical comparison, decay-based temporal scoring is implemented elsewhere, validity-aware legal filtering is prescribed and partially implemented, and a leading legal benchmark states that in-force status of retrieved provisions is not assessed. Residual uncertainty concerns publication value rather than factual overlap.
rationale: The challenge search found the validity/bitemporal framing and a temporal-validity-filtering legal RAG already published, while the closest legal framework paper reports no empirical comparison, leaving measurement rather than concept as the apparent residual gap.
resolution: Resolved: the post-hoc temporal re-ranking component cannot be positioned as a distinct contribution. Decay-based temporal scoring is already implemented (learnable exponential decay inside graph-based retrieval), validity-aware retrieval is already prescribed and partially implemented as an ontology-driven pre-retrieval filter, and the requirement and even its detection criterion are articulated in the legal-retrieval literature - which nonetheless reports no benchmarked empirical comparison of existing systems. The defensible delta is the implemented measurement: version-level point-in-time recovery and contamination on near-duplicate amended clauses with recency-decoupled strata, plus the comparative finding about whether the published recency-decay hybrid suffices. Caveat to state honestly in any write-up: the metric is conceptually prescribed by prior work, so the contribution is evidence and implementation, not formulation.
